questions.question: Define the significance of Porbandar in Gandhi’s early life.
questions.solution_html:
• Porbandar, Gandhi’s birthplace, played a significant role in shaping his early life and cultural
  • values. Its traditional Gujarati environment and family influences helped lay the foundation for
  • his moral principles and later philosophy.
questions.final_answer: his moral principles and later philosophy
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Mention the major areas in which women participated during the Gandhian period.
questions.solution_html:
• Major areas of women's participation during the Gandhian period: Women participated in
  • the freedom struggle through non-cooperation, civil disobedience, the Salt Satyagraha, and the
  • Quit India Movement. They also promoted khadi, picketing of foreign cloth and liquor shops
  • and social reform activities.
questions.final_answer: and social reform activities
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Define the meaning of civilisation according to Gandhi in Hind Swaraj.
questions.solution_html:
• Meaning of civilization according to Gandhi in Hind Swaraj: Gandhi defined true civilization as
  • a mode of conduct that teaches people to perform their duties and follow the path of morality.
  • He believed that civilization should promote self-control and moral development rather than
  • material comforts.
questions.final_answer: material comforts
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Define the moral significance of earning one’s livelihood through labour according to Gandhi.
questions.solution_html:
• Moral significance of earning one's livelihood through labour: Gandhi considered earning
  • one's livelihood through physical labour a moral duty and a means of self-reliance. His idea of
  • bread labour teaches that everyone should perform physical work to earn their living and
  • respect the dignity of labour.
questions.final_answer: respect the dignity of labour
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: State one important Gandhian norm for the eradication of untouchability.
questions.solution_html:
• One important Gandhian norm for the eradication of untouchability: Gandhi advocated
  • treating all human beings equally, irrespective of caste, and opposed discrimination against
  • untouchables. He encouraged equal social rights and access to public places, temples, and
  • other common facilities.
questions.final_answer: other common facilities
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: State Gandhi’s view of religion in relation to Ramarajya.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi's view of religion in relation to Ramrajya: Gandhi understood Ramrajya as a kingdom
  • of righteousness based on truth, justice, non-violence, and moral values. He did not consider it
  • a Hindu state but an ideal society where people of all religions enjoy equal rights and freedom.
questions.final_answer: a Hindu state but an ideal society where people of all religions enjoy equal rights and freedom
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: State the role of fearlessness in Gandhi’s ethical thought.
questions.solution_html:
• Role of fearlessness in Gandhi's ethical thought: Gandhi considered fearlessness an essential
  • virtue for practising truth and non-violence. It enables individuals to resist injustice and
  • oppression without fear of suffering or punishment.
questions.final_answer: oppression without fear of suffering or punishment
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: State the contribution of women to the Quit India Movement.
questions.solution_html:
• Contribution of women to the Quit India Movement: Women participated in demonstrations
  • strikes, underground activities, and the dissemination of nationalist messages during the Quit
  • India Movement. Leaders such as Aruna Asaf Ali and Usha Mehta played significant roles in
  • sustaining the movement.
questions.final_answer: sustaining the movement
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Define craftsmanship according to Gandhi.
questions.solution_html:
• Craftsmanship according to Gandhi: Gandhi regarded craftsmanship as the development of
  • practical skills through productive manual work. He emphasized learning through handicrafts to
  • promote self-reliance, dignity of labour, and the all-round development of individuals.
questions.final_answer: promote self-reliance, dignity of labour, and the all-round development of individuals
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Define truth according to Mahatma Gandhi.
questions.solution_html:
• Truth according to Gandhi: Gandhi considered truth to be the highest moral principle and
  • closely identified it with God. He believed that individuals should practise truthfulness in their
  • thoughts, words, and actions.
questions.final_answer: thoughts, words, and actions
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: State the meaning of Sarvodaya in Gandhian thought.
questions.solution_html:
• Meaning of Sarvodaya in Gandhian thought: Sarvodaya means the welfare or upliftment of
  • all. Gandhi advocated a just and non-violent society that promotes the well-being of every
  • individual, especially the poor and disadvantaged.
questions.final_answer: individual, especially the poor and disadvantaged
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the importance of local self-government in Gandhi’s Grama Swaraj.
questions.solution_html:
• Importance of local self-government in Gandhi's Grama Swaraj: Gandhi considered local
  • self-government essential for village autonomy, democracy, and self-reliance. He envisioned
  • village panchayats managing local affairs through people's participation, cooperation, and
  • collective responsibility.
  • short essay.
questions.final_answer: short essay
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the moral significance of means in the attainment of social and political ends according to Gandhi.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi believed that means and ends are inseparable, and good ends can be achieved only
  • through righteous means. He rejected violence, dishonesty, and exploitation as methods of
  • achieving political or social goals. According to him, truth and non-violence are essential means
  • for establishing a just and peaceful society.
questions.final_answer: for establishing a just and peaceful society
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain Gandhi’s criticism of the cultural and intellectual consequences of foreign language education in India.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi criticised foreign language education, especially English education, for distancing
  • Indians from their mother tongues, culture, and traditions. He believed that it created an
  • intellectual gap between educated Indians and ordinary people. He advocated mother-tongue
  • education to promote cultural identity, independent thinking, and wider access to knowledge.
questions.final_answer: education to promote cultural identity, independent thinking, and wider access to knowledge
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the role of non-violence in Gandhi’s theory of trusteeship.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi's theory of trusteeship holds that wealthy people should use their wealth for the
  • welfare of society rather than for selfish interests. Non-violence encourages the voluntary
  • sharing of wealth and the peaceful resolution of economic inequalities. It seeks social justice
  • through moral persuasion and cooperation rather than force or violent class conflict.
questions.final_answer: through moral persuasion and cooperation rather than force or violent class conflict
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the principle of learning through productive activity in Gandhian Basic Education.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi's basic education, known as Nai Talim, emphasises learning through productive
  • crafts and practical activities. It integrates intellectual development with physical work, moral
  • education, and the development of practical skills. This approach promotes self-reliance, dignity
  • of labour, and the all-round development of children.
questions.final_answer: of labour, and the all-round development of children
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the importance of village industries in achieving economic decentralization.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi considered village industries essential for creating employment and strengthening
  • rural economies. They promote local production, reduce dependence on large-scale industries
  • and encourage the equitable distribution of wealth. Thus, village industries support economic
  • self-sufficiency and decentralisation of economic power.
questions.final_answer: self-sufficiency and decentralisation of economic power
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the relationship between truth and non-violence in Satyagraha.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi regarded truth and non-violence as the two fundamental principles of Satyagraha.
  • Truth provides the moral objective, while non-violence serves as the means of pursuing it
  • without harming opponents. Together, they enable people to resist injustice through peaceful
  • and morally responsible action.
questions.final_answer: and morally responsible action
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Compare Gandhi’s conception of true civilization with the ideals promoted by modern civilization.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi understood true civilization as a moral way of life based on self-control, duty
  • simplicity, and ethical conduct. In Hind Swaraj, he criticised modern civilization for its excessive
  • emphasis on material comforts, machinery, and endless wants. He believed that genuine
  • progress should be measured by moral development rather than material advancement.
questions.final_answer: progress should be measured by moral development rather than material advancement
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the positive and active character of Gandhi’s non-violence.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi's non-violence is not merely the absence of physical violence but an active
  • expression of love, compassion, and courage. It requires individuals to resist injustice and
  • oppression through peaceful means. Therefore, non-violence involves active moral struggle for
  • truth, justice, and social transformation.
questions.final_answer: truth, justice, and social transformation
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the role of non-violence in maintaining a democratic society according to Gandhi.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi believed that non-violence strengthens democracy by promoting tolerance, mutual
  • respect, and peaceful disagreement. It enables citizens to oppose unjust laws and government
  • actions without resorting to violence. According to him, a genuine democracy depends on
  • public participation, moral responsibility, and respect for the rights of others.
questions.final_answer: public participation, moral responsibility, and respect for the rights of others
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the relationship between social duties and Varṇadharma.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi interpreted Varnadharma as the performance of duties associated with one's social
  • role and emphasised the dignity of honest labour. He believed that individuals should serve
  • society through their work and fulfil their responsibilities without selfishness. However, his
  • views on varna evolved over time, and he strongly opposed untouchability and discrimination
  • based on caste.
  • Essay
questions.final_answer: Essay
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain Gandhi’s nationalist strategy based on Satyagraha, Ahimsa, mass mobilisation, and non-violent resistance, and assess its significance in India’s freedom struggle.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi's nationalist strategy was based on Satyagraha, which means resisting injustice
  • through truth and non-violent action. Ahimsa, or non-violence, served as the moral foundation
  • of his political struggle. He mobilised people from different sections of society through
  • movements such as the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and Quit
  • India Movement. His methods encouraged mass participation and challenged British rule
  • without relying on armed violence. This strategy played a significant role in strengthening
  • national unity, spreading political awareness, and advancing India's struggle for independence.
questions.final_answer: national unity, spreading political awareness, and advancing India's struggle for independence
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Compare and critically discuss Gandhi’s principle of Swadeshi with economic dependence on foreign goods, highlighting its ethical and national significance.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi's principle of Swadeshi encouraged people to use locally produced goods and
  • support indigenous industries. He believed that dependence on foreign goods weakened India's
  • economic independence and harmed village industries. Swadeshi promoted self-reliance
  • dignity of labour, local employment, and the revival of traditional crafts, especially khadi
  • production. However, in the modern world, complete economic isolation may limit access to
  • useful technologies and essential goods, making balanced economic cooperation necessary.
  • The ethical and national significance of Swadeshi lies in encouraging responsible consumption
  • strengthening local economies, and promoting economic independence without rejecting
  • beneficial international exchange.
questions.final_answer: beneficial international exchange
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Compare Gandhian ideals with contemporary challenges such as consumerism, / social conflict, environmental degradation, and communal divisions.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi's ideals of simplicity and self-restraint offer an alternative to consumerism and
  • excessive materialism. His principle of Ahimsa encourages peaceful conflict resolution, mutual
  • respect, and dialogue in society. His emphasis on simple living, local production, and limited
  • wants provides guidance for addressing environmental degradation and the overuse of natural
  • resources. Gandhi's commitment to religious tolerance and equality is relevant to reducing
  • communal divisions and promoting social harmony. Thus, Gandhian values remain significant
  • for building a peaceful, sustainable, and morally responsible society.
questions.final_answer: for building a peaceful, sustainable, and morally responsible society
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss Gandhi’s views on the importance of mother tongue as the medium of education and explain its educational significance.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi believed that the mother tongue should be the primary medium of education
  • because children understand concepts more easily in their own language. He criticised
  • excessive dependence on English education for creating cultural alienation and separating
  • educated people from the masses. Mother-tongue education encourages independent thinking
  • creativity, cultural awareness, and effective communication. It also makes education more
  • accessible to children from different social and economic backgrounds. Therefore, Gandhi
  • considered education through the mother tongue essential for intellectual development
  • cultural preservation, and national self-reliance.
questions.final_answer: cultural preservation, and national self-reliance
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

  • educated people from the masses. Mother-tongue education encourages independent thinking
  • creativity, cultural awareness, and effective communication. It also makes education more
  • accessible to children from different social and economic backgrounds. Therefore, Gandhi
  • considered education through the mother tongue essential for intellectual development
  • cultural preservation, and national self-reliance.
questions.final_answer: cultural preservation, and national self-reliance
